subject: washing machine
title: What If You Never Cleaned Your Washing Machine?

scenes.text: What if you never cleaned your washing machine? It cleans your clothes. So what cleans it?
Cool washes, liquid soap and a shut door leave the rubber seal and soap drawer damp for days.
Over months, bacteria move in. Thirteen home machines in Germany held 229 different kinds of bacteria.
That musty smell has a source, Moraxella osloensis. It turned up in nine of the thirteen door seals.
In one German hospital, a washer kept passing a drug-resistant germ onto newborns' knitted hats and socks.
No baby got sick, and the germ vanished once that machine was removed. The thing that washes needs washing.

description:
What if you never cleaned your washing machine? A Furtwangen University study found 229 kinds of bacteria in 13 home machines, with the musty-smell bacterium Moraxella osloensis in nine of the 13 door seals.
In a German hospital, a household washer passed a drug-resistant Klebsiella strain to newborns' knitted hats and socks until it was removed.
